review_comments.body: Instead of just commenting on required properties put a comment above line 332 with a link to current requirements. Then everything below the comment will be ensuring alignment with those requirements.
I thought this was required for strict mode, did that change?

comments.body: It's still required: strict mode needs `additionalProperties: false` on every object, and the request we send still carries it (the encode tests now assert that, and the cassettes are unchanged). What changed is the snapshot: it records the user's `format.schema`, which we used to mutate in place and now deep-copy, so the flag no longer leaks into it. I also replaced the comment with a single one above the block linking to OpenAI's supported-schemas requirements (daccb2b).
Thanks, that clears it up. The docs link and the assertion on the outgoing schema address my comments. The snapshot change makes sense now. This looks good to me.
